landability_note: Both remedies are backend-only Rust edits confined to reality-server source files, no migration and no client/openapi regen. F1 (price_map input validation): mirror the existing time_window closed-match 400-rejection for `mode` (accept only {sale, rent}) and optionally for `property_type` (accept only the documented enum), returning StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST with a message naming the allowed values — verifiable via `cargo build -p reality-server` plus a unit test asserting GET /api/v1/price-map?mode=bogus returns 400 (currently 200 with empty districts + a poisoned-but-bounded cache entry). F2 (password-reset timing uniformity): make the UserNotFound branch do constant-work equivalent to the Sent branch (e.g. perform a throwaway token hash / fixed artificial delay) so the two code paths are not trivially distinguishable by response latency — verifiable via a focused unit/bench test comparing the wall-clock of the found vs not-found path, or simply by code review that both branches execute the same hashing work.

evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/price_map.rs:230 — `let mode = query.mode.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "sale".to_string());` accepts ANY string for the `mode` query param with no validation, then binds it directly as `transaction_type = $1` (line 343). The docstring on PriceMapQuery.mode (line ~182) says 'sale or rent', but nothing enforces it. An arbitrary `?mode=foo` silently produces an empty `districts` result with HTTP 200 and `mode: "foo"` echoed in the response body (PriceMapResponse.mode, line 374), and the empty result is cached under that key for the full 1h TTL.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/price_map.rs:238-253 — this is INCONSISTENT with the sibling `time_window` param in the SAME handler, which IS strictly validated via a closed `match` that returns `StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST` ('Unsupported time_window {:?} — expected one of 1m, 3m, 12m, 5y') for any unrecognised value. The author's own comment at line 231-233 states the design intent: 'reject unsupported values up-front rather than silently falling back. Otherwise the response echoed back an invalid time_window even though the data was computed for a different interval.' That exact rationale applies verbatim to `mode` (and to `property_type`, bound at line 344 as `($2::text IS NULL OR property_type = $2)` with no enum check), yet neither gets the 400 treatment.

Severity LOW (+1): no injection (mode/property_type are bound parameters $1/$2, never interpolated into SQL text) and no OOM (the cache is bounded at MAX_PRICE_MAP_CACHE_ENTRIES=10_000). Impact is a correctness/consistency gap: an invalid `mode` returns a misleading empty-but-200 response echoing the garbage value instead of a 400, and burns a cache slot. Confidence medium: the missing validation and the divergence from the time_window handling are confirmed by static read of a single handler; whether clients send bad `mode` values is usage-dependent. NET-NEW: the prior price_map findings in the corpus are code-review-reality-server-price-map-cache-unbounded (cache memory bound, DONE) and code-review-reality-server-assertsqlsafe-format-sql (SQL-safety of the AssertSqlSafe opt-out, DONE) — neither covers query-param input validation, and price_map.rs was last touched by PR #3146 (2026-10-25) after the previous reality-server review pass (2026-10-22).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/handlers/users/mod.rs:541-585 — `request_password_reset` is response-enumeration-safe (the route at routes/users.rs:520-560 maps BOTH Sent and UserNotFound to a generic HTTP 200), but it is NOT time-uniform. The UserNotFound branch early-returns at line 554 (`None => return Ok(PasswordResetRequestResult::UserNotFound)`) immediately after the single `find_user_by_email` lookup. The Sent branch then does strictly more work on an existing account: `reset_repo.invalidate_user_tokens(user.id)` (DB write, line 558-560), 32-byte CSPRNG fill + base64 encode + sha256_hex (lines 565-573), and `reset_repo.create(...)` (second DB write, line 574-580). Two extra DB round-trips plus hashing make the found-account path measurably slower than the unknown-email path — an observable timing side-channel (CWE-208) that lets an attacker enumerate which emails are registered despite the uniform 200 status.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/users.rs:550-560 — the `Ok(PasswordResetRequestResult::UserNotFound)` arm only emits a `tracing::debug!` with an email_log_hash and returns the generic 200; it performs NO compensating/dummy work (no throwaway hash, no fixed delay), so there is nothing equalising the two code paths' latency. The response-body/status uniformity the handler was explicitly designed for is thus undermined by the timing differential.

Severity LOW (+1): no auth bypass, no data exposure in the response; exploitation requires statistical timing analysis over the network and yields only account-existence, the same class of information already tracked for the register path (code-review-reality-server-register-account-enumeration, response-based, DONE). This finding is the TIMING residual on the DISTINCT password-reset endpoint, which that prior finding does not cover. Confidence medium: the asymmetric work (early return vs 2 DB writes + hashing) is confirmed by static read; the real-world distinguishability depends on network/DB noise, so it is a latent side-channel rather than a runtime-measured one.
